_comment: Backfill for r20261105-0803 (bench 4: the telcoin-network main branch with PR 1783's lazy protocol negotiation and nine instrumentation commits, on v2 operator scripts with every observer trusted by every validator and one coordinated start; one blast, index 0, chaos on; metrics from the run's own bench-obs Prometheus), published with: make_bundle.py --run r20261105-0803 --compare r20261103-1922 --backfill benchmark/report/backfill/2026-11-05-main-v1lazy-obs.json. Sources (field by field in benchmark/private/bench4-r20261105-0803/P/backfill-notes.md): the run manifest (harness, node_probe, node_startup, consensus_parameters, admission, coordinated_start, chaos, chaos_schedule, chaos_schedule_refresh, chaos_boundary, phases, blasters, obs, prom_window, fleet_ready, timestamps, deploy_runs, notes), metrics.json (Prometheus 15 s from bench-obs, 08:37:58Z to 10:20:29Z, plus Cloud Monitoring 60 s), the generators' results, the samplers, the eleven nodes' unit logs, the analysis units A1 (KPIs and windows), A2 (certification and vote path), A3 (chaos, recovery and boundaries), A4n (census and node-side bottlenecks) and A4o (timeline, faults, defects), the live run record, and telcoin-network commits a0d6e6e26, a4e55c880 and 496ebefb5. recovery: node, killed_utc, restarted_utc, rejoined_utc and catch_up_secs equal what make_bundle computes from the node-mode metric (rejoined 10:15:13Z, 2,160 s), so merge_recovery keeps them silently; failed_reports (0) comes from validator-05's own log and fills the computed null (no seal-failure series for that node). The log's own times (rejoin 10:14:58.184, catch-up 2,152 s, restart to rejoin 2,168 s) are in the caveats. harness is not set: harness_block uses the manifest's record (d6a8d53, dirty) and ignores the backfill. generator.analysis_sha is left to make_bundle.
title: The main branch with lazy protocol negotiation and vote-path instrumentation
summary: We repeated the 40-minute chaos run of 3 November (r20261103-1922) on the same fleet, ten c3-highcpu-8 validators with Hyperdisk Balanced disks, one in each of ten regions, and an observer, with a node built for the benchmark from the main branch, the lazy protocol negotiation of PR 1783 and nine commits of vote-path, execution and recovery instrumentation, and with metrics on the run's own Prometheus server. With all ten load generators running, average chain throughput was 4,578 tx/s, against 4,037 tx/s on r20261103-1922 and 5,434 tx/s on r20261007-0316; the chain produced 15.8 blocks a second over the mixed phase, the median time for a transaction to land was 3.3 s and the 95th percentile 12.84 s (3.49 and 14.17 s on r20261103-1922), and throughput stayed flat from one five-minute block to the next instead of falling. Lazy negotiation made every vote one network round trip instead of two: the idle round fell to the 350 ms minimum header delay, and every validator, London and the Netherlands included, certified at least 99.6 % of its own headers while the chain was idle (5.2 % and 5.0 % for those two on r20261103-1922). Throughput was bound by execution: every node's execution engine was busy about 98 % of the loaded time at a flat cost of about 215 µs per transaction, a ceiling of about 4,600 tx/s, and persisting each output to disk was no longer the part that grew. Two validators that were not chaos targets, Hong Kong from 09:20 and Singapore from 09:27 UTC, left the committee under load: their engines, waiting on slower database syncs than the rest of the fleet's, queued longest, their own consensus commits fell 41 rounds behind the certificates they received, one past the limit at which a validator is demoted, and their load generators landed nothing from then on. With validator-05 killed at 09:33:50, 60 s before an epoch close, the committee was left with exactly the seven voters a quorum needs, which cost a 17-second commit pause; the epoch closed on time. The restarted validator-05, like Singapore, then went through the promotion and demotion loop of r20261103-1922 again (13 and 21 promotions, each from an empty DAG with a stale header) and held its place only when epoch 6 began, 2,168 s after its restart; Hong Kong held from the start of epoch 5. Every epoch record reached quorum on every node active at the close, but two of them were signed by exactly seven validators.

evidence_detail: Commit 496ebefb is the head of the public branch bench/main-v1lazy-obs-2026-11, built for this benchmark from the telcoin-network main branch at a0d6e6e26 (#1761, 4 November). On top of main it carries the four commits of PR 1783, which make every outbound substream negotiate with multistream-select V1Lazy (a4e55c880: a dialer that proposes exactly one protocol sends the proposal and its request in one flight instead of waiting a round trip for the listener's confirmation) and complete and test the gossipsub fallback (dc1ad5f1d, bbd0880ef, e6d85bd68), then nine instrumentation commits, eight features and one follow-up fix (496ebefb5), that add the log lines and Prometheus series this run's analysis reads: the voter's vote path by stage, the proposer's vote round trips, header storage and the proposal lock, the engine's execute, persist and commit timings and its busy time, rejoin blockers and node-mode transitions with their reasons, the scheduled leader of every round and its outcome, batch-serve denials and denied batch requests, epoch-record signers and missing signers, and outbound request durations by service class. The run named the image by registry digest (adiri@sha256:f6922184…, pushed as adiri:bench-main-v1lazy-obs-20261104). The build contains the certifier fix of r20261006-0458 (cfc9e34f, #1579) and the consensus-storage rework (#1558). Against r20261103-1922's v0.2.0-devnet build 3f9b0709 it has 29 commits that build lacks and lacks 19, and the two differ in 206 files. r20261007-0316's lazy negotiation came from a different commit (b0838dd38), which is not in this build's history.

fleet.label: c3-highcpu-8 + Hyperdisk Balanced (c3-hdb), ten regions, validator-05 in Ashburn

load.placement: one blaster per validator, in that validator's zone, sending only to it

methodology: The node image was built for this benchmark from the branch bench/main-v1lazy-obs-2026-11 (telcoin-network main plus PR 1783 and nine instrumentation commits) and named by registry digest (sha256:f6922184…), so there was no tag to resolve. Before creating anything the harness ran that image to confirm that it reports telcoin-network 0.1.0 built from commit 496ebefb, has the sub-second timestamp fork active from genesis and contains the log messages later checks rely on, and it recorded the committed consensus parameters file, unchanged from r20261103-1922: maximum header delay 1,000 ms, minimum header delay 350 ms and maximum batch delay 250 ms.

The instrumentation commits fix the shape of the log lines and series the analysis reads, so no figure on this page depends on parsing free text: per vote, the voter's time in each stage (vote lock, validation, the wait for its own execution, parents, leader, batches, store, persist) and any vote timeout with its stage; per vote request, the proposer's round trip, attempt and the header's age; per header, its store and send times; per round, the scheduled leader and whether it was swapped or found; per consensus output, the engine's queue wait, execute, persist and commit times; per subscriber decision, why a rejoin was not yet possible and why a node changed mode; per epoch close, who signed the epoch record and who was missing; and per request-response exchange, its service class and duration, with matching Prometheus counters and histograms.

Preflight checked access, tools, quotas and a clean genesis directory, and confirmed the load-generator image built from tn-transaction-generator commit 3911723, the generator of r20261103-1922. The results were merged and sized with that repository's aggregate.py and derive-sizing.py at commit 4434bac, which reproduces every published KPI of r20261103-1922, r20261007-0316 and r20261006-0458 exactly.

The harness created ten validators and one observer on c3-highcpu-8 (8 vCPU, 16 GB), each with a 100 GB Hyperdisk Balanced boot disk provisioned at 20,000 IOPS and 800 MiB/s, one validator in each of ten regions (Los Angeles, London, Sydney, Tokyo, Ashburn, the Netherlands, Singapore, Hong Kong, Seoul and Mumbai) with the observer in Los Angeles, the zones of r20261103-1922; every node was created on the first attempt. It also created a separate metrics VM for the run (bench-obs, e2-standard-4, 50 GB, in Los Angeles) running Prometheus and Grafana; it collects metrics only, no logs.

Each node's keys were generated on the node by the operator scripts of the v0.2.0-devnet release (tn-node-deployment d9446f7, the v2 scripts), four nodes at a time, with each node advertising its RPC endpoint on its internal address (r20261103-1922 advertised unresolvable placeholder names). The harness built genesis for a separate benchmark chain (chain id 32286, 20-minute epochs). Before any node started it installed on every node a network configuration in Closed admission mode that names every validator and lists the observer as trusted by every validator, so that no fleet member refuses another (on r20261103-1922 only validator-01 trusted the observer).

Each node was finalized by the release's scripts, four at a time, run alone just long enough to show that the service started and answered RPC, and stopped again. While every node was stopped, one session per node wrote the benchmark settings into its start script: RPC and websocket listening on all interfaces, a local metrics endpoint, a 20 GB rotation size for the node's log file, and the log filter info,primary=debug,engine=debug,subscriber=debug,worker::network=debug,network::reqres=debug with the primary's certificate validator, manager and fetcher at info. No per-node consensus override was set.

All eleven nodes were then started at one due time, 08:22:35 UTC: every node began in that second (spread 0 s, none late) on the first attempt. Each node's metrics agent was then pointed at bench-obs with the benchmark network label; no node was restarted for it. The devnet's shared observability VM was not used by this run and received none of its samples or logs.

A verify-only pass read back from each running node its chain id, consensus progress, start-script settings, parameters file and boot lines; all eleven had logged commit 496ebefb, the three consensus delays, the 5,000 ms vote timeout and the sub-second fork from genesis, and passed by 08:35:25 UTC; an on-node sampler was then started on each. The health and admission gate, which finished at 08:37:58 UTC, found Prometheus on bench-obs answering with all eleven nodes reporting under the benchmark network and no devnet series, all ten validators active, and on every node admission mode 2 (Closed) on the primary and the worker network, no fallback and no denied connection in either direction; a read of the ConsensusRegistry confirmed the 1,200 s epoch duration.

It deployed the devnet contract set that the mixed workload calls, from 08:37:58 to 08:49:03 UTC, over a single ssh port-forward to validator-01's RPC that held for the whole run. The chain was then idle, apart from the deployment, until the funding step at 09:01:37.

A one-off funder VM funded 600 sender accounts for each of ten load generators from 09:01:37 to 09:03:03 UTC. The generators, on e2-standard-2, one per validator in that validator's zone and sending only to it, started together at 09:08:29 UTC: a preamble of setup transactions (10 to 15 s per generator, none resent), 120 s of warm-up, 2,400 s of mixed load across 13 transaction types and up to 180 s of cool-down, cut short after 30 s in which none of the generator's own transactions landed. All ten mixed phases began within 6 s of each other. No network delay was injected.

The chaos schedule was timed to the chain's epochs. The harness read the ConsensusRegistry at a pinned block (block 180, epoch 2), chose the close of epoch 3, and re-read the schedule once epoch 3 had opened (09:17:29 UTC, drift 0 s). It staged three actions on the target nodes, each to fire on the node's own clock: bench-validator-05's container killed with SIGKILL 59 s before that close, due at 09:34:49 UTC, and held down, the node restarted 300 s after the kill, and the observer's node restarted 300 s after that. The kill began at 09:33:50.164, the restart at 09:38:50.179 and the observer restart at 09:43:50.061, each less than 0.2 s after its planned second; the closing commit came at 09:34:50, so the outage crossed the boundary. Before the kill and the observer restart each node saved its own container log.

During the run the harness sampled the fleet's highest block; the only period without a new block it recorded, 09:51:00 to 09:54:30 UTC, is the end of the load (the last transaction block is at 09:50:54), not a stall.

Afterwards the harness collected each generator's results and the on-node sampler files, then waited until every validator read active again and stayed active for 180 s before closing the metrics window (886 s of waiting, to 10:17:26 UTC). It pulled 60-second machine metrics from Cloud Monitoring and 15-second node metrics from bench-obs's Prometheus over a local forward (08:37:58 to 10:20:29 UTC), with no series missing; the collection finished at 10:21:34 UTC.

The KPIs and windows on this page come from the publishing pipeline's own window and KPI steps, run through the driver that reproduced the published figures of the three comparison runs. Rounds per second come from each node's round counter and from the generators' block streams. Certification, the vote-path breakdown, leader shares, the execution split, rejoin and mode changes and the epoch-record quorum come from the instrumented log lines and series above, read from every node's complete unit log (all eleven nodes, the whole run) in one streaming pass each, with the engine's per-block debug dumps dropped.

Teardown saved every node's container log, its unit log file, sampler files and service journal before deleting anything. The unit logs were about 49 GB each uncompressed, so the pulls, four at a time over IAP at about 2 MB/s each, took from 10:22 to 14:41 UTC; the streams of five nodes were restarted from zero, three after a transport fault and three after a name-resolution failure on the machine running the harness. The post-pull check then refused to delete, because it treated the pull records it had just written as stale; every saved file was checked by hand against its recorded size, and a second teardown at 14:42:31 trusted those records and accepted all eleven. A restart of the operator's session ended that run at the certification step at 14:52 UTC with nothing deleted, and a third run, started detached, continued from there. That third run passed every gate and pulled the Prometheus snapshot, then its first instance delete failed because the installed gcloud rejects --async on instance deletes; after the harness fix a fifth run deleted all 12 instances, the two firewall rules, the bucket and the disks (TEARDOWN_DONE deleted=12 left=0 at 17:19:37Z), and the results directory was re-indexed (251 files, 91.4 GB).
caveats: The comparison run, r20261103-1922, had the same fleet in the same zones, the same load generator, load shape and chaos plan, the same consensus timing (1,000/350/250 ms) and the same operator scripts. The node build differs: this run's 496ebefb is the main branch with lazy protocol negotiation and the instrumentation commits, where r20261103-1922 ran the v0.2.0-devnet release 3f9b0709 with strict negotiation; the two differ in 29 and 19 commits and 206 files. The deployment differs in admission (here every validator trusts the observer, so no connection was denied; there the observer was refused by nine validators), in the RPC addresses the nodes advertise, and in a much heavier log filter (next caveats). Against r20261103-1922, average chain throughput with all generators running rose from 4,037 to 4,578 tx/s, blocks a second over the mixed phase from 13.47 to 15.84, the median time to land fell from 3.49 to 3.3 s and the 95th percentile from 14.17 to 12.84 s, while primary rounds a second fell from 1.07-1.09 to 0.84-0.91. No difference can be assigned to any one change.

Two validators that were not chaos targets left the committee under load, mid-epoch: bench-validator-08 (Hong Kong) at 09:20:07 UTC and bench-validator-07 (Singapore) at 09:27:01. This was not a committee rotation: every epoch record names all ten validators. Each node's own consensus commit had drifted behind the committee, Singapore's from the start of the load at about 2 s a minute and Hong Kong's from the epoch-2 close at 09:14:49 at about 6 s a minute, until a certificate arrived 41 rounds above its committed round, one past the 40-round activity window, and the node demoted itself to follower ('we are behind', reason outside_gc_window). Their proposers were still at the frontier, but their votes had become late and then stopped. Hong Kong held active again from the epoch-5 entry at 09:54:55 (two promotions, one failed); Singapore went through the promotion loop of the next caveats 21 times and held only at the epoch-6 entry at 10:14:56. Tokyo's commit drifted the same way, to about 10 rounds, and stayed active; every other validator stayed within 0.2 s.

Their load generators, 08 and 07, each send only to their own validator, which refused every send while inactive ('validator is inactive'): generator 08 landed none of its transactions after 09:20:06 and generator 07 none after 09:27:02, and generator 05 none after the kill at 09:33:50. The all-generators window (09:10:46 to 09:50:40 UTC) is therefore the window in which all ten generators ran, not one in which all ten landed: ten lanes landed in its first 9 minutes and seven in its last 17. Chain throughput did not fall as the landing set shrank (4,433 tx/s with ten, 4,515 with nine, 4,672 with eight and 4,646 with seven), because the chain was execution-bound (below).

The per-validator ranges on this page cover the nine validators other than the chaos target, so they include bench-validator-07 and -08 although both were inactive for most of the mixed window; their resources are those of nodes that had stopped voting. Their commit latency sets the high end of the commit-latency p95 range (30 s each); Tokyo is next at 23.7 s and the other five read 8.0 to 8.4 s, with medians of 1.12 to 1.19 s. bench-validator-10 has no commit-latency series, so that KPI covers eight nodes. The values are interpolated within the histogram's coarse upper buckets.

With Hong Kong and Singapore out, the kill of validator-05 left seven voting validators, exactly the 7-of-10 quorum, from 09:33:50 until Hong Kong returned at 09:54:55, so every certificate in that time needed every remaining vote. The kill paused commits for 17 s (leader round 1,144 at 09:33:50.2, the next at 09:34:07.4), and the chain had its longest gap of the run without a block, 19 s from block 24,434 at 09:33:50 to 24,435 at 09:34:09; r20261103-1922's kill, with nine voters left, paused nothing. Chain throughput across the outage stayed at 4,050 to 5,002 tx/s a minute and epoch 4 opened on time.

Validator-05 restarted at 09:38:50 UTC, found itself an epoch behind 14 s later and followed the chain as an inactive member. Under load it did not gain: its engine was busy all the time and executed 700 to 1,000 blocks a minute while the chain made about 920, so it fell from 4,797 blocks behind at 09:38 to 7,092 at 09:49 and stayed 236 to 308 rounds behind the newest header, far outside the 20-round rejoin window. It reached the chain head only about ten minutes after the load ended, entered epoch 5 six minutes after the fleet, and was promoted for the first time at 10:00:59. That promotion and the eleven after it failed as on r20261103-1922: each started from a DAG restored empty, re-proposed a stale stored header that every peer refused as too old (257 refusals), made no execution progress, and was demoted 7 to 9 s later when the committee was 41 rounds ahead; each demotion was followed by about 60 s without progress until the sync path re-requested the missing range, a cycle of 70 to 73 s. It held only at the epoch-6 entry, 10:14:58, when every node starts again from round 1: 2,168 s (36 min 8 s) after its restart and 2,469 s after the kill to its first own certificate (r20261103-1922: 2,170 and 2,471 s). Its load generator landed nothing for the last 1,012 s of its mixed phase and ended with 6,918 of the run's 7,677 unlanded transactions.

The recovery record on this page takes its rejoin time (10:15:13 UTC) and catch-up duration (2,160 s) from the 15-second node-mode samples; validator-05's own log puts the switch to catch-up mode at 09:39:05.8 and the rejoin at 10:14:58.2, 2,152 s. The failed-report count (0) is from the log, which has no batch-seal failure after the restart; the node has no seal-failure series in the metrics. The 15-second gauge also misses promotions that last less than a scrape: it shows 7 of validator-05's 13 promotions and 13 of Singapore's 21. The comparison runs' recovery figures were published from other sources (r20261103-1922's from its log), so the catch-up comparison is not exactly like for like.

Execution bounded throughput. Over the loaded time every node's engine was busy 976 to 988 ms in each second, its queue of consensus outputs sat at its cap of 8, and on validator-01 an output waited 7.3 s at the median (11.1 s at the 95th percentile) before it began executing. Per output, executing took about 75 % of the engine's time and persisting it 24 %, most of that the database commit's sync; the cost per transaction stayed about flat, 185 to 231 µs and about 215 µs through most of the load (execute 138 to 166, persist 45 to 64), while outputs grew with the rounds, which at 98 % busy is a ceiling of about 4,600 tx/s, the chain's own rate. On r20261103-1922 persisting was 60 to 72 % of the busy time and the cost per transaction rose from 160 to 310 µs, so throughput fell block over block; here the five-minute chain rate stayed between 4,179 and 4,829 tx/s, and the telcoin process wrote 131.6 MiB/s at the median (439.3 MiB/s there). A validator also waits for its own execution before it votes and before consensus emits each committed sub-DAG, which ties the engine back into the round.

Hong Kong and Singapore did not execute more slowly than the rest; they persisted more slowly. Before the drops their database commit took 533 and 420 ms at the median against 305 to 364 ms on the other validators, their engine queue waits reached 15.3 and 14.5 s at the 95th percentile (Tokyo 13.6 s, the others 10.0 to 11.3 s), and Hong Kong's disk wrote 28 % more bytes a second at a third of the IOPS, with I/O pressure at 11.4 % against 6.7 to 7.5 %; CPU was no higher on either. The observer, in the same zone as validator-01, whose disk was normal, showed the same slow-sync signature and cannot be demoted, so the cause is most likely variance between disk volumes of the same type, but that has not been measured.

Every vote now takes one network round trip. Over 72 proposer-voter pairs, a vote's round trip less the voter's own service time equals the pair's measured UDP round trip at the median (ratio 1.00), and the request reaches the voter without waiting for a protocol confirmation, where r20261103-1922 measured 2.02 round trips. Idle, the round settled at 352 ms, the 350 ms minimum header delay (451 ms on r20261103-1922), each proposer's quorum formed with its sixth-fastest vote plus 4 to 6 ms, and every proposer certified 99.6 to 100 % of its headers. London's and the Netherlands' quorums, at 264 and 273 ms, still arrive after the other proposers have moved to the next round, so 70.6 and 70.2 % of their idle certificates were never committed and they led 0.2 % of the idle rounds. Some paths no longer match the October probe used as the reference: London and the Netherlands to Singapore, Hong Kong and Mumbai now take 1.26 to 2.26 times the probed round trip in both directions, and the probe has no row for Ashburn.

Under load the vote is slow because of the voter, not the wire. The voter's wait is its own execution: before voting, a validator waits until it has executed the block the header names (95th percentile 930 ms over the fleet), and the same proposer's later requests queue behind that wait on the vote lock; fetching parents and batches took at most 1 ms at the 95th percentile. Voters whose execution kept up (Sydney, the Netherlands, Seoul, Mumbai) answered within 90 to 183 ms at the 95th percentile; Los Angeles, London and Ashburn waited 0.85 to 1.45 s, and Tokyo, Singapore and Hong Kong rejected 21 to 62 % of their requests after the wait. Rounds lengthened as voters dropped out: the mean committed round took 806 ms with ten voters, 1,047 ms with nine, 1,185 ms with eight and 1,458 ms with seven after validator-05's restart, against 346 ms idle with all ten after the rejoins, and about a third of loaded rounds ended on the 1 s maximum header delay.

Both loaded epoch boundaries left the chain 13 s without a block (09:14:49 and 09:34:50 UTC), against 12 and 26 s on r20261103-1922: a node starts the next epoch only after executing the old one through its closing block, and this run's execution backlog at the close was 4 to 10 s (19 to 22 s there). The observer, which serves no load, detected the epoch-3 close 21 s after the validators. Every epoch record reached quorum, with no timeouts, on every node that was active at the close (one timeout on validator-05 at the epoch-2 close); late or inactive nodes fetched the finished record from a peer. The epoch-3 and epoch-4 records were signed by exactly seven of the ten validators, the quorum with no margin. The five 'failed to reach quorum on epoch close' errors in the logs (two inside the metrics window) all come from a node whose collector missed the first broadcast of peer votes and never retried; each of those nodes had the finished record from a peer, so liveness was not affected.

The leader schedule kept naming validators that were not taking part. Of 669 scheduled leader rounds under load, 42 (6.3 %) were not committed, 40 of them because the leader's certificate never reached the DAG (Seoul 17, 13 of them before any demotion; Hong Kong 11 and Singapore 5 after theirs); after the load 246 of 1,704 (14.4 %) failed, half for validator-05 and half for Singapore, each costing a leader timeout. The three inactive members also kept receiving every header and refused 53,344 vote requests as too new. London and the Netherlands led 4 and 5 of 1,958 idle rounds (the reputation schedule swaps them out) and more under load.

No validator ran short of batch-serving capacity under load: the batch-serve pool never filled and no serve was denied on any node (r20261103-1922: 1,560 denials, sustained, to the far validators). The 1,148 batch-sync streams refused at open fell almost all in 8 s after the epoch-2 close (09:15:03 to 09:15:11 UTC), almost all of them Singapore's, which had asked every peer at once and overran the per-peer limit, plus Tokyo's.

The log filter of this run puts the execution engine at debug level, which logs a full dump of every executed block and every consensus output. Under load that wrote about 1.16 GB a minute per validator, 99.7 % of the bytes, and each validator's unit log reached about 49 GB over the run; each node's root disk, which also holds the database, went from 7 to 65 % full. The log appends added about 25 to 45 MB/s, 15 to 25 % of each node's disk writes, and doubled the write IOPS; they did not slow the database commit on the validators that stayed active. The CPU (mean 32.2 to 35.2 % against 19.1 to 20.8 % on r20261103-1922), disk and write figures on this page include this logging, which no production node does, and have not been corrected for it.

Resident memory of the telcoin process grew from 1.2 GB idle to 8.0 to 9.7 GB by the end of the load on 16 GB machines and held there, with no memory pressure and no out-of-memory event; a longer load could reach the limit. The disk throttle series were unavailable from Cloud Monitoring, the samplers record I/O pressure as 'some' only, and bench-validator-09's persist histograms are empty in the metrics, so its persist split comes from its log.

The 99th-percentile time to land of four generators (Sydney, the Netherlands, Seoul, Mumbai) reads about 300 s, interpolated inside the latency histogram's 256-to-600 s bucket, so it says only that a small tail took minutes; the run-wide 99th percentile is 31.38 s (443.43 s on r20261103-1922).

The node metrics on this page come from the run's own Prometheus on bench-obs, scraped every 15 s and read at the end of the load; the snapshot of that Prometheus taken at teardown is not used. Earlier the same day the first launch of this benchmark had stopped at its preflight gate, because the devnet's shared observability VM, where earlier runs sent their metrics, was filling with the live devnet's own debug logs; the run waited 7 h 26 min while those logs were given a 24-hour retention and the devnet nodes were set to info-level file logging, and then ran on its own metrics VM. No sample or log line of this run went to the shared VM.

The teardown saved every node's logs before it deleted anything, but its post-pull check refused to proceed because it applied a 15-minute freshness rule to the pull records it had written itself over four hours; every saved file was checked against its recorded size and the re-run trusted the records. During the pulls a name-resolution failure on the machine running the harness restarted three streams from zero, and a later restart of the operator's session ended the re-run at its certification step; neither touched the nodes or the saved files, and all the analysis on this page reads only the saved files.

The harness is recorded at commit d6a8d53, marked dirty; the only uncommitted change was a notes file in the operator-scripts submodule's working tree, which no step reads. The coordinated-start record carries the time it was written (08:30:13 UTC), not the start, which its due time puts at 08:22:35. The final wait for every validator to read active lasted until the epoch-6 entry, because Singapore and validator-05 could rejoin only there; it changes the metrics window, not the load. No node was restarted outside the chaos plan.
This configuration has been run once, so run-to-run variation is not measured.
